reason: The cited evidence shows that preheating to 200 °C is used to minimize residual stresses (E2) and that lack of preheating causes cracking (E4), but no evidence supports the specific 250–300 °C range, its effect on grain refinement, or the claimed improvements in dimensional precision and mechanical integrity for AlCoCrFeNi. E1 discusses rapid cooling in laser cladding but does not address preheating, and E3 only generally notes that high preheating may attenuate cracking.
premises: Elevated build-plate preheating (250–300 °C) reduces thermal gradients and residual stresses in SLM of AlCoCrFeNi.
Reduced thermal gradients lead to a finer, equiaxed grain structure.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stresses decrease fabrication-induced defects (porosity, cracking, distortion).
Improved dimensional precision and mechanical integrity result from the above microstructural and stress improvements.
A preheating temperature of 200 °C (baseline) is insufficient to achieve these benefits.
